ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A composite conductor consists of three conductors of radius \( R \) each. The conductors are arranged as shown in the figure. The geometric mean radius (GMR) (in cm) of the composite conductor is \( kR \). The value of \( k \) is ______.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: There are three identical circular sub-conductors in the figure, each radius labeled R. The centers of the three circles are connected by dashed lines, forming a triangle; the center distance between the upper two sub-conductors is labeled 3R, and a 60° angle is given in the figure, indicating that the three centers form an equilateral triangle. Therefore the center distances of the three pairs of sub-conductors are all d12 = d23 = d31 = 3R. Then reasoning: The composite conductor contains n = 3 sub-conductors. The self GMR of each solid circular conductor is 0.7788R. The composite conductor GMR is taken as the 1/9 power of the 3×3 ordered distance product: the three diagonal terms are 0.7788R, and the six off-diagonal mutual distance terms are 3R. So GMR = [(0.7788R)^3(3R)^6]^(1/9) = R[(0.7788)^3·3^6]^(1/9). Therefore k = [(0.7788)^3·3^6]^(1/9) ≈ 1.91.

The six ordered mutual log terms are ln(3R), since the center triangle is equilateral with side 3R. Therefore ln(kR) = [3ln(0.7788R)+6ln(3R)]/9.
